description: One event on a Calendar's schedule. Times are ISO datetimes read in the calendar's timeZone, never the reader's. Calendar draws the chip; the consumer writes one of these per event and Calendar settles where it goes.

id.description: Stable identity, so a host can switch on it rather than on the title.

colorId.description: Identity colour. Give the same entity the same slot everywhere and it keeps its colour across views.

actionsEnabled.description: Whether the chip shows its action button. A boolean rather than "is the actions slot filled?", for the reason Alert.dismissible and Toast.dismissible already record: Angular cannot detect whether an ng-content was filled, so gating the drawing on that is a divergence waiting to happen.

actions.description: The action panel's content, revealed by the chip's action button. Rendered only while the panel is open, so a consumer's own controls never sit permanently in the grid's Tab sequence.

disabled.description: Whether the chip is drawn but cannot be activated — an event a consumer's rules lock, such as one already past or owned by someone else. It reflects through `aria-disabled` rather than the native `disabled` attribute, so the chip keeps its place in the grid's roving Tab sequence and is announced as unavailable instead of disappearing from it. With no `click` there is nothing to disable and the chip is inert already.

click.description: The chip was activated. No payload: the consumer wrote this element, so they already hold the event this is about. Never emitted while `disabled`.
